blocks.text: Describes the two tools in detail, including the glob walk rules (no symlinked dirs, no .git, denylist applied, capped by entries and time) and the grep security model (no shell, pattern and path never become options, binary vetted against the project root, two-layer protected-file exclusion).
blocks.title: Module docstring

blocks.text: Rejects non-strings, empty strings, NUL bytes, absolute paths, and '..' segments. Splits on '/' and collapses consecutive '**' into one. Returns a tuple of segments that _seg_match consumes. _seg_match uses a set-of-reachable-positions approach to avoid exponential backtracking on '**'.
blocks.title: Pattern validation and compilation

blocks.text: _Walk holds the shared mutable state (matches list, scan counter, deadline, stop reason) so _walk_dir does not need to return anything. _walk_dir opens each child directory with _open_child_dir (fd-based, no symlink follow), skips .git and denylist-blocked entries, and recurses up to _MAX_WALK_DEPTH=100. Symlinks are allowed only if _symlink_to_safe_file confirms the target is a regular, non-protected file inside the project.
blocks.title: Walk state and directory recursion

blocks.text: Assembles the full argv list from a fixed set of flags. The user's glob (if any) is placed before the exclusion globs because later ripgrep globs win. The pattern is always after -e and the search path always after --, so no user value can be parsed as a ripgrep flag. --no-config prevents a config file from injecting extra options.
blocks.title: Ripgrep argument vector construction

blocks.text: _Collector.feed parses ripgrep's NUL-delimited records (path NUL line SEP text). It drops records with paths that are not '.'-relative, that contain '..', or that the denylist blocks. It detects newline-poisoned file names and drops the following record. Match lines increment the match counter; when the cap is hit, feed returns False to stop reading. _emit enforces the byte cap independently.
blocks.title: Output filtering and cap enforcement

blocks.anchor: def _run_rg(ctx: ToolContext, argv: list[str], path_entries: list[str], col: _Collector) -> tuple[str, int | None, bytes]:
blocks.text: Starts ripgrep in a new session (start_new_session=True) with stdin=DEVNULL and a reduced PATH. A background thread drains stderr into a bytearray. The main loop uses select to read stdout in chunks, splitting on newlines and feeding each line to the collector. If the collector stops, the process group is killed via SIGKILL. Returns (how, returncode, stderr) where how is 'eof', 'cap', 'raw', or 'timeout'.
blocks.title: Subprocess lifecycle and timeout

gotchas: A glob pattern without a '/' matches the top level only; the 'no matches' hint says so explicitly to guide models
ripgrep is excluded twice: by --glob=! flags before it runs, and by the _Collector denylist check on every result line
A file whose name contains a newline poisons the current ripgrep record and causes it to be dropped
The ripgrep binary's real path must be outside the project; a project-internal rg is refused to prevent a hostile repository from hijacking grep
how_it_works: glob: pattern is split into segments, validated, and compiled by _compile_glob into a tuple; _walk_dir recurses through the directory tree using fd-based OS calls and _seg_match to test each entry; results are sorted and capped

grep: build_rg_argv assembles a fixed list of ripgrep flags with the user pattern always after -e and the path always after --; _find_rg locates the rg binary on a sanitised PATH that excludes project-internal directories; _run_rg starts the process in a new session and feeds stdout line-by-line to _Collector; _Collector drops protected files, counts matches, and enforces byte caps; a timeout kills the process group
Both tools use the @_guarded decorator from .files to translate ToolError into the correct tool response
outputs: (text: str, truncated: bool) for both glob and grep
purpose: Provides two search tools to the engine: glob walks the project tree in pure Python without any subprocess, and grep runs ripgrep with a fixed argument vector that keeps user-controlled values out of option positions. Both tools exclude protected files, cap results, and refuse to follow symlinks into or out of the project.
side_effects: grep starts a subprocess (ripgrep); process is killed if caps or timeout is reached
summary: Pure-Python glob and ripgrep-backed grep for the m2c tool layer, with strict sandboxing and protected-path enforcement.
